images.title: Letters as a counting sequence
images.purpose: Shows counting with the letters a to z: the 20th object gets t, and a 27th object has no letter left.
images.composition: Plain white background, the main object large and centred with wide empty margins, no scenery, no characters, no extra decoration. One long row of square letter tiles running left to right, with two short pointers above it and one empty dashed tile at the right end.
images.exact_structure: A row of square tiles with white fill and dark outlines, left to right: tile a, tile b, tile c, then three small grey (#6B7280) dots, then tile t with a teal (#0072B2) fill and white letter, then three small grey dots, then tile z, then one dashed vermilion (#D55E00) empty tile holding a vermilion question mark. Exactly 6 solid tiles and 1 dashed tile. Above tile t, a short teal pointer labelled 20th. Above tile z, a short grey pointer labelled 26th. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Letters can count in order, but after z they run out.
images.description: Shows counting with the letters a to z: the 20th object gets t, and a 27th object has no letter left.
images.context: Worked example: the 20th object is t; with 27 objects there is no letter.

image_decisions.why: The limit of letters is best seen as a sequence that simply stops after its 26th tile.
